.surfaces.

langfuse.label: Langfuse (self-hosted or cloud)
langfuse.host_note: Self-hosted Langfuse serves on http://localhost:3000 by default (plain http unless you put TLS in front of it); Langfuse Cloud: https://cloud.langfuse.com (EU), https://us.cloud.langfuse.com (US), https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com (JP), https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com (HIPAA).

copilot.note: There is NO Langfuse plugin for Copilot. Copilot CLI/VS Code export OpenTelemetry natively; Langfuse is an OTLP backend (HTTP/JSON or protobuf; gRPC is not supported).

optional.OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSA: true - OPT-IN, off by default: stores prompts, responses and tool arguments in Langfuse. VS Code-launched CLI sessions forward the enable flag and endpoint but not this one.

copilot.debug: COPILOT_OTEL_EXPORTER_TYPE=file writes spans locally to confirm they are generated before pointing at Langfuse

dash0.label: Dash0 (OpenTelemetry)
dash0.host_note: Dash0 is a hosted service - there is no localhost default. The OTLP URL is on the Dash0 Endpoints settings page (OTLP via HTTP tab), shaped like https://ingress.<region>.aws.dash0.com. A local Docker collector (Jaeger/Prometheus) is NOT Dash0 - choose 'Another backend' for that.

copilot.note: No Dash0 plugin for Copilot (Dash0's docs only mention Copilot as reading DASH0_TEAM_NAME). Dash0 does accept OTLP, so Copilot's native OpenTelemetry export could be pointed at it, but that setup is not verified here - record provider + host and wire it by hand from Dash0's docs.

other.label: Another tracing backend
other.note: Record provider + host only. se-harness installs nothing for this choice; the user wires it up.

figma_design_system.note: only when org has a Figma design system (B11)

choose_one: Sourcegraph (sourcegraph/sourcegraph - hosted MCP; Cloud or self-hosted instance)
structural.note: A7 bake-off pending — the first three are MCP servers configured via .mcp.json, not marketplace plugins. Two unrelated projects share the 'CodeGraph' name: codegraph-ai/CodeGraph (tree-sitter semantic graph, 42+ MCP tools, RocksDB persistent memory layer, VS Code extension) vs colbymchenry/codegraph (lightweight pre-indexed graph, CLI-installed, SQLite, native OS file-watcher auto-sync, no external services) — confirm which repo the user means before installing. colbymchenry/codegraph installs via: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colbymchenry/codegraph/main/install.sh | sh (macOS/Linux) or npm i -g @colbymchenry/codegraph, then `codegraph install` + `codegraph init [path]`. codebase-memory-mcp has its own installer: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/main/install.sh | bash. Graphify is CLI + skill based, not MCP-first: PyPI package is `graphifyy` (double-y; the CLI command stays `graphify`) — install via `uv tool install graphifyy` (or `pipx install graphifyy`), then `graphify install --project` to register a project-scoped `/graphify` skill (committable), or a graphify platform install to also wire the PreToolUse hook that nudges (or, with `--strict`, blocks-once-per-session) raw file reads toward `graphify query` instead — a natural pairing with se-harness's own hook-enforced gates. Local tree-sitter AST parsing for code, no vector store; docs/PDF/image/video ingestion calls the assistant's model API. An `.mcp.json` route exists too if MCP access is preferred over the skill: `uv tool install "graphifyy[mcp]"` then `python -m graphify.serve graphify-out/graph.json`. The other drivers have their own commands too: /harness-mem-codebase-memory (install with confirmation, explicit client registration instead of the installer's auto-config of ~45 clients, per-repo index, optional cross-repo-intelligence linking, refresh), /harness-mem-codegraph (colbymchenry: install, init, register with the callers/callees/impact tools enabled, telemetry choice; codegraph-ai: register and verify only), /harness-mem-sourcegraph. If Graphify is chosen, se-harness's own /harness-mem-graphify command (not this registry entry's install line) is what /harness-bootstrap hands off to for the actual install-plus-first-build — it also handles merging multiple repos' graphs into one workspace-level graph, which a bare Graphify install doesn't do on its own. Sourcegraph is a REMOTE MCP server (Streamable HTTP) hosted by the Sourcegraph instance itself: nothing is installed locally and no index is built by se-harness - the instance indexes its connected repos, so the repo(s) must already be on it. Requires an Enterprise plan with MCP enabled (admin setting mcp.enabled, default true) and the MCP#ACCESS permission. Two deployment shapes, one config: Sourcegraph Cloud (a managed single-tenant instance, URL given by Sourcegraph) or self-hosted (your own https URL); the public sourcegraph.com site is not what this entry is for. Endpoints: <url>/.api/mcp (search, navigation, repos, history; the default) or <url>/.api/mcp/all (adds Deep Search). Auth: OAuth (interactive browser login, no secret on disk - recommended for people) or an access token with the mcp scope sent as 'Authorization: token <value>' (for headless use; the value lives in .env.harness as SOURCEGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN, only its name is ever written to a committed file). Tools include keyword_search, nls_search, go_to_definition, find_references, read_file, list_files, list_repos, commit_search, diff_search, compare_revisions. Because it searches every repo on the instance in one query it suits large multi-repo workspaces and replaces the per-repo index plus merge step that Graphify needs. /harness-mem-sourcegraph connects (user-scope or per-repo .mcp.json, or the Copilot equivalents), verifies and reports which workspace repos are on the instance; /harness-bootstrap hands off to it. It builds no index. Docs: https://sourcegraph.com/docs/api/mcp
